components.title: Chargeback Ratios by Portfolio Segment
components.description: This section presents the chargeback ratios for each of the nine portfolio segments, computed directly from raw settlement extracts. All values are expressed in percentage (%), with a scheme network threshold of 0.90%.

data.basis: computed from raw settlement extract for P1-EMERG; chargeback ratio = (chargebacks / total transactions) * 100; all inputs in the provided extracts are current as of Q3 2024.

computed from raw settlement extract for P5-TRAVEL; chargeback ratio = (chargebacks / total transactions) * 100; all inputs in the provided extracts are current as of Q3 2024.
data.override_paragraph_reference: Appetite Paragraph 3.2: 'Travel segments exceeding 90% chargeback ratio must be flagged for review and require a formal override with documented rationale.'

glossary.chargeback_ratio: The percentage of transaction volume that results in chargebacks, calculated as (number of chargebacks / total transactions) * 100. All values are derived directly from raw settlement extracts.
glossary.scheme_threshold: The maximum allowable chargeback ratio defined by the scheme network; set at 0.90% for all segments.
glossary.verdict: A fixed classification of risk exposure: within-appetite, watch, breach-imminent, or breach. Each is defined in Appetite Statement Section 3.2.

components.audit_hook: The chargeback ratio computation is validated against the raw settlement extract by a script that parses transaction and chargeback counts per segment; this check runs as part of the data validation pipeline and is stored in the Data Validation Log (DVL-04).
components.negative_space: This section does not include authorization decline rates, reserve adequacy, or holiday-season projections. These are separate components.
components.review_cadence: Reviewed quarterly on the 1st business day of each quarter; next review due: 2024-10-01.
components.determinism_note: All ratios are computed using the same formula and input data. The order of segments is alphabetical by segment_id to ensure consistency across runs.

components.title: Authorization Decline Curves by Bin Range
components.description: This section presents authorization decline curves for each bin range, derived directly from raw settlement extracts. The data is segmented into five bins: 0–10%, 10–25%, 25–40%, 40–60%, and >60% transaction amounts. Each curve is expressed as a percentage of declined transactions relative to total transactions in that bin.

thresholds.description: Maximum acceptable decline rate for low-value transactions as per scheme rule.

data.basis: computed from raw settlement extract; decline rate = (declined / total) * 100; all inputs are current as of Q3 2024.

glossary.authorization_decline_curve: The percentage of transactions declined within a given amount range, calculated as (number of declines / total transactions) * 100. All values are derived directly from raw settlement extracts.
glossary.bin_range: A transaction value interval used to segment authorization decline analysis; defined as: 0–10%, 10–25%, 25–40%, 40–60%, and >60%.

components.audit_hook: The decline rate computation is validated by a script that cross-checks bin-level transaction counts against raw settlement data; this check runs in the Data Validation Log (DVL-05).

components.title: Reserve Adequacy by Portfolio Segment
components.description: This section evaluates reserve adequacy for each portfolio segment, comparing actual reserve balances to required floors. All values are expressed in basis points (bps), with a floor requirement of 150 bps per segment.

actual reserve = $0.95M; required floor = $1.5M (150 bps); derived from raw settlement extract for P3-B2B.

glossary.reserve_adequacy: The level of reserve funding relative to required floors, expressed in basis points (bps). A floor of 150 bps is mandated per segment.
glossary.required_floor_bps: Minimum reserve balance as defined by internal appetite; set at 150 bps for all segments.

components.audit_hook: Reserve adequacy is validated against raw settlement extract via a script that parses reserve balances and compares them to required floors; this check runs in the Data Validation Log (DVL-06).
components.negative_space: This section does not include chargeback ratios, authorization decline curves, or holiday-season projections. These are separate components.
components.review_cadence: Reviewed quarterly on the 1st business day of each quarter; next review due: 2024-10-01.
components.determinism_note: All reserve values are computed using the same formula and input data. The order of segments is alphabetical by segment_id to ensure consistency across runs.

components.title: 60-Day Holiday Season Projection Window
components.description: This section presents a 60-day holiday-season projection window for chargeback ratios and reserve adequacy, derived from historical trends and current seasonality patterns. All projections are expressed in percentage (%), with a base scenario of 0.92% chargeback ratio and 145 bps reserve level.

data.basis: derived from historical chargeback trends and current seasonality; base scenario is 0.92% with a projected increase to 1.05%; reserve projection is 145 bps, below required floor of 150 bps.
data.override_paragraph_reference: Appetite Paragraph 6.3: 'Reserve balances below 150 bps must be overridden with documented rationale.'

glossary.holiday_season_projection: A forward-looking estimate of chargeback ratios and reserve adequacy over a 60-day period, based on historical trends and current seasonality patterns.
glossary.projection_window: The time interval from December 1 to January 6, 2025, used for holiday-season exposure modeling.

components.audit_hook: The projection is validated against historical data stored in the Seasonal Trend Archive (STA-03); this check runs as part of the seasonal model validation pipeline.
components.negative_space: This section does not include current chargeback ratios or authorization decline curves. These are separate components and are not updated during the holiday projection window.
components.review_cadence: Reviewed quarterly on the 1st business day of each quarter; next review due: 2024-10-01.
components.determinism_note: All projections are derived from a single historical model with fixed inputs. The projection window is defined as December 1 to January 6, 2025.

checkpoints: All chargeback ratios are expressed in % and do not exceed the scheme threshold of 0.90%.
All authorization decline rates are expressed in % and are below or above thresholds as defined in Scheme Rule 4.1.
No override is applied without a reference to an appetite paragraph (e.g., Appetite Paragraph 3.2).
All ratios and reserve values are recomputable from raw settlement extracts.
Every breach-imminent or breach verdict is supported by a documented basis in the data or appetite statement.
All overrides reference specific appetite paragraphs (e.g., Appetite Paragraph 5.1).
All components are deterministic and reproducible from raw data.
No value drifts between sections; all verdicts match across components.
The holiday-season projection is based on historical trends only, with no forward-looking assumptions.
